doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Driving limousines and school buses to get by
summary: Gates describes part-time driving jobs in Connecticut while starting out in music, including the junior high school bus.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Did you have your grub stake to see you through for a while?

I was still trying to — I was working part time. I was driving a limousine, I was driving a school bus, whew. That was a tough date, driving a school bus. No I drove just about everything with wheels. But the freight on a school bus is difficult to deal with. Livestock is easier. I don’t know, electrical appliances are easier.
What grade level were you driving?

Oh, they called it junior high. Seventh and eighth grade. I mean when I went to school it was seventh and eighth grade it wasn’t junior high, you went to grammar school and then you went to high school. But junior high, these kids are like, they don’t even know if they’re standing up or sitting down or laying down, their hormones are all over the place. They’re just nuts. And you know, I want quiet when I drive. Yeah that’s going to happen. So I mean I would do a gig on the weekend and be like lifted. And then Monday morning, 6:30 a.m. there’s kids on the bus screaming and I’m going, “I just did this and now I’m doing this.” So it brings back some reality. It makes you realize that this is the planet earth, you’ve got to deal with some other stuff. I didn’t get plucked and they put me on Carnegie Hall. And that’s a good thing.
